text:
maya: Quick question — the permissions preview currently doesn't reflect routing policy quotas. e.g. showing a role has 'invoke' rights but not that route is rate-limited to the tenant. How should we surface that?
aj: We hit this during the canary. Product wants a single effective preview that includes routing/quotas.
chris: Do we mean show quota as a read-only affix on the effective permission? or a separate panel that shows policy fallout? :thinking:
zara: Separate panel seems clearer. If you dump routing into the same line it's misleading. Example: Tenant A can call model X but only 10 rps, so effective access depends on quota.
maya: Agree separate panel. But UX asks for 'what-if' — admins want to test "if I remove role Y, will route fallback to shared pool and break SLA?"
leo: Implementation-wise we can compute effective view server-side by combining: role bindings + route policy + quota buckets. API endpoint could be `GET /v1/preview/effective-permissions?principal=...&route=...`
chris: That endpoint needs to be idempotent/cheap. Running the full router evaluation for every preview could be heavy. Maybe cache snapshots per route-policy-version.
aj: Telemetry note: if we add this preview we should tag previews with `preview=true` in logs to avoid polluting usage. Also sampling at 10%.
zara: UX asks for a diff view: show current vs. simulated change. So preview should return a list of delta items like `+can_invoke(10rps)` or `-can_burst`.
maya: Example response sketch (for devs):
```json
{
  "effective": ["invoke:model-x:allowed:10rps"],
  "diff": ["if remove role Y -> invoke:model-x:allowed:shared-pool (may throttle)"]
}
```
leo: For quotas we need to surface both per-tenant hard limit and fallback routing policy. Two separate fields: `quota` and `fallback_route` in the preview response.
chris: Also edge-case: service accounts with scoped tokens — they bypass certain tenant quota shapes. Need to include principal type in preview output.
aj: Ops ask: show rollout impact. If canary is enabled, preview should accept `policy_version=canary` param. That way support can simulate pre-rollout state.
maya: UX microcopy: we should warn when preview depends on ephemeral canary policy: "Preview uses canary routing rules; actual behavior may change after rollout."
zara: Also show telemetry links: "View route telemetry" linking to console chart for the last 24h. That helps admins decide.
leo: Implementation plan: 1) new preview API 2) snapshot cache keyed by (route, policy_version, principal_scope) 3) preview UI panel with diff + telemetry link 4) sampling & `preview=true` telemetry.
chris: Dev concern: snapshot invalidation. Snapshots must be invalidated when routing policy or quota configs change. We can emit a `snapshot:invalidate:route:{id}` event.
aj: Security check: ensure preview respects read-only scopes. Only principals with `preview:read` can call the API. Default tenant admins get it.
maya: Can we show an inline quick-grant from the preview panel? Product wants a one-click 'grant temp access' button tied to an audit log.
zara: Fine but it must create an approval log entry. Also enforce TTL on quick-grant.
chris: For the quick-grant API, propose `POST /v1/admin/grants` body: `{ principal, route, permission, ttl, note }`. Audit middleware will add actor info.
leo: Deploy note: I'm going to push canary of the preview API to staging tonight. deploy-bot: canary deploy started for service=authz-preview, version=2026.03.21-rc1 :rocket:
aj: Small perf test: generate 500 previews against staging with cached snapshots — measure p95. If >200ms we need to tune.
maya: Okay team — I'll draft the UI panel copy and wireframe. tagging @zara for microcopy review and @chris for API contract. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary complete for service=authz-preview, instance=3/3, status=healthy :white_check_mark:
